top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock rests on a distinct physical step, magic-wavelength trapping that cancels the light shift so many neutral atoms can be interrogated together, which separates it from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. It is reproduced at the 10^-18 level by independent laboratories (RIKEN/Tokyo, JILA, NIST, PTB, SYRTE), with theory and measurement tied through a controlled systematic budget, and has opened many-body clock physics, millimetre-scale redshift tests and bounds on varying constants. The two-name allocation (Katori for the proposal and first demonstrations, Ye for the accuracy and many-body programme) is the most defensible on the slate, though I accept the priority record for Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow and Oates is unverified. A prize now is better than no award.
